title: How Donkey Kong Toppled Atari
summary: This article examines how Nintendo's Donkey Kong arcade game, ported to the Atari 2600 in 1982, became a catalyst for Atari's decline and the broader video game crash of 1983. The rushed, low-quality port exposed Atari's poor quality control and business practices, while Nintendo's superior arcade experience highlighted the growing gap between console and arcade quality.
problem_solved: Documenting how a single game port exposed Atari's systemic quality issues and contributed to the 1983 video game crash.
why_valuable: Provides historical lessons about product quality, platform holder responsibilities, and how third-party mismanagement can destroy an entire industry.
